title: Better standardize the initialization of stat taps
description:
1. Have the stat taps initialization callback include a boolean return value
2. Use that boolean return value to determine the success/failure of an individual stat tap
3. Use cmdarg_err to output a message to the user when the stat tap fails to register
4. If a stat tap registration fails, exit the application from the stat_tap_ui "layer", not the tap itself. exit() should generally be used only by internals to keep consistent behavior.

Ping #20432

Better to choose an exit code from include/ws_exit_codes.h ?
Probably.  To me some of the question is "Do we even want an exit?"  I really didn't like the exit() within the taps, but this matches previous functionality (that should rarely happen).
I suppose if we are running tshark, this is all the user asked for and we can't give it to them, so should exit.  For Wireshark it might make more sense to acknowledge the error but keep going.

It would probably look better to continue to "bubble up" the failure (to have it specifically exit in tshark.c), but that would break the API of start_requested_stats().  Unsure if that would make waves (I'm guessing it's not a popular reused function)

changed this line in [version 4 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/19601/diffs?diff_id=1330220712&start_sha=738b2d82ddf95e44a212c0b96e86525026b8dcdb#b9e37d8e97844d60438efc88ecfceff274b365a8_144_144)

After looking at README.developer, I don't think start_requested_stats() would be an API we should be concerned about breaking, so I made the change to have it return success/failure and have tshark appropriately exit if it fails (and Wireshark will continue to silently ignore it)

Michael - I assumed this is ready so merged?

I think so... I've fallen down two different rabbit holes of
1. Helping work towards #20432 
2. Wanting to refactor where exit() is used, because I think it's used at the wrong layer in several places (taps being one of them).

I think this patch includes the correct "scope" for the tap cleanup, but I kept finding more exit() calls and trying to figure out what to do with them.  At this point, I think it should be separate patches.

Better standardize the initialization of stat taps

1. Have the stat taps initialization callback include a boolean return value
2. Use that boolean return value to determine the success/failure of an individual stat tap
3. Use cmdarg_err to output a message to the user when the stat tap fails to register
4. If a stat tap registration fails, have the application layer (i.e. tshark) to decide on the "exit", not the tap itself. exit() should generally be used only by internals to keep consistent behavior.
